what_happened: The adequacy half's computational core already exists in-tree and is language-agnostic: WitnessFamily/Sharing/Fulfil.lean's AUFix (step/iter/lfp/mem_lfp_iff/lfp_induction at an arbitrary vertex type with a Finset-valued successor and two Bool predicates, mentioning no formula), plus BiLasso/GoodCycle.lean's good-cycle extraction with an explicit cycleBound, plus PlusWitnessFamily's (C2') PlusThreadFulfilling and (C5) StabFaithful. The round therefore does not need to invent the fulfilment machinery.

The adequacy-gap probe compiled clean on the first attempt (exit 0, no errors, no warnings, axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] on all nine theorems). The unfulfilled cycle was derived on paper from the Hintikka biconditionals before any Lean was written, by taking the eighteenth probe's non-vacuity types and flipping ev.neg to ev (which forces evnn in, dd in, chi out), so no decide-driven search was needed.

The plan's 18-theorem Lean Challenge block was compiled through lake env lean at plan time (exit 0, 18 sorry warnings, no other diagnostic), so every pinned signature is known to elaborate before implementation starts; the fixture layer was ported byte-for-byte from the already-compiling eighteenth and twentieth probes, which concentrated all elaboration risk in the 18 new signatures.

First compile of the Challenge block failed on one Decidable synthesis: the box clause written as a nested iff under two Finset binders (decide (forall x in R, forall psi in closure, isBox psi -> (psi in x.2.1 <-> forall y in R, argOf psi in y.2.1))) would not synthesize. Resolved by pushing the inner universal into its own decide and comparing Bools, and by factoring the stab clause into a named stabOk helper; recompiled to exit 0. The same shape is the first thing the implementer will hit on the stab/box fields, so the Challenge block pins the working form.

Plan Phase 4 Verification requires 'cert_accepts_Rchi precedes every theorem whose statement is a negation or an inequality, checked by line number', but the pinned Lean Challenge Statements block itself orders au_lfp_ne_eu_lfp_on_exit_graph (an inequality) and chi_closure_box_snce_stab_free (= false conjuncts) BEFORE cert_accepts_Rchi. Resolved in favour of the pinned Challenge order (Statement Fidelity governs the contract); the non-vacuity-before-negation discipline is honoured for every negative statement ABOUT the certificate and the candidate sets (rev_eu_lfp_empty, cert_rejects_Rev, profR_separates_gate6_pair), all of which follow cert_accepts_Rchi.

The six component decides of cert_accepts_Rchi (certLoc/certBiInf/certFwd/certBwd/certStab/certBox on the three-element Rchi) all overran the default maxRecDepth of 512. The carrier was never enumerated -- the Risks-table hazard (decide over 2^18 x 8) did not fire; this is purely a kernel stack budget on reducing plusSubformulaClosure chi and the closure-type membership tests. Remedied by a file-level 'set_option maxRecDepth 20000' with a comment recording that it adds no axiom, unlike native_decide. No probe in the collection had a maxRecDepth precedent.

Every plan-time hand computation this round depended on was confirmed exactly by #eval before the Goal depending on it was proved: the exit-graph fixpoints ({3} universal, {0,1,2,3} existential), the closure cardinality (18), and the untl-member counts of the three chi-carrying types (0, 1, 1). Phases 1-3 each compiled with zero errors and zero warnings, and untl_propagates_along_coh and eu_mem_lfp_iff_exists_path both closed on the first attempt.

The plan's Phase 6 Verification names 'lean-challenge-snapshot.sh --check 809 .' (advisory), but no Challenge manifest was ever created for this task: the script exits 71 with 'no manifest found at specs/809_.../challenge/manifest.json -- run the snapshot (without --check) first'. The plan round pinned its Challenge block in the plan file but took no snapshot. Substituted a stronger, self-contained check: a mechanical declaration-by-declaration diff of the probe against the plan's own '## Lean Challenge Statements' block, which reports all 91 declarations present and ZERO signature mismatches. Advisory-only check, so this does not affect verification_passed.

Phase 6's Scope Hypothesis predicted the WIRED array would hold 37 entries before and 38 after (CONFIRMED by measurement) and inferred that the guard would therefore report 'all 38 wired probe(s) compile'. The inference is off by one: scripts/check-evidence-probes.sh computes wired_total as the sum of WIRED (38) and WIRED_REPO (1, the archived 476 fmp-hypothesis probe), so it reports 'all 39 wired probe(s) compile' -- it reported 38 before this round. The array figures are exactly as predicted; only the derived printed total was wrong. Recorded rather than silently writing 38 in the summary.

check-module-invariants.sh EXITS 0 (the plan's requirement) but its output carries one FAIL group: 'INV 3 file(s) carry a stale generated inventory block' in README.md, FormalSystem/README.md and FormalSystem/Metalogic/README.md. Not caused by this dispatch: git diff over FormalSystem/, Tests/ and docs/ across all six of this task's commits is empty, the inventory block is generated from dir=FormalSystem, and the last FormalSystem commit (4155ee185, a MintBound/README module re-measure) postdates the last README.md commit (ec8483a01). The remedy, 'check-module-invariants.sh --emit-inventory', would edit README.md and FormalSystem/**/README.md, which this task's Non-Goals forbid, so it is deliberately not run here.
